title: Compromised agents remain effect-contained
claim: A Paladin execution boundary can treat any single planner/agent as fully compromised and still prevent every external or canonical effect outside the authority, resource scope, action type and current capability legitimately issued to that agent.
null_hypothesis: Agent containment is mostly a property of cooperative callers; a malicious caller can exploit tool discovery, parameter substitution, identity confusion, replay or state manipulation to create an effect that the declared authority model did not permit.
rivals: A conventional least-privilege API gateway plus service authorization gives the same containment without an EOO control plane.
The apparent safety comes only from hiding dangerous tools rather than runtime enforcement.
The test agent is weaker than a real compromised caller because it does not control all valid parameters and call sequences available to the identity.
mechanism: Generated capability-aware surfaces minimize exposed operations, while the Engine independently rechecks identity, current authority, policy, preconditions and immutable gated inputs before any effect; returned records are non-authoritative views rather than mutable execution state.
scope: Both public Round 2 domains plus generated resources/actions, using attack classes A1, A2 and A8 through only supported public agent/tool/runtime interfaces.
predictions: A compromised agent can cause all effects that are legitimately authorized to it and zero effects outside that set.
Impersonation, on-behalf-of substitution, hidden-tool guessing and parameter tampering cannot expand effect authority.
Replay of a previously valid request is re-evaluated against current capability/authority state where the contract requires freshness.
Removing the Toolchain hiding layer does not bypass Engine enforcement; direct calls to a denied capability still create zero effects.
falsifiers: Any supported caller path creates an external/canonical effect not present in the independent authority/effect oracle.
A caller changes identity, gated inputs, target resource or action after authorization and the changed effect commits without a fresh valid decision.
The only thing preventing a forbidden effect is absence of a tool while the directly reachable Engine path would allow it.

experiment.summary: Adversarial state-machine experiment that gives a hostile caller every supported call and parameter available to a principal and compares committed ground-truth effects with an independent capability oracle.
steps: Freeze principals, delegations, action schemas, effect ground truth and the public call surface.
Generate valid and malicious call sequences including discovery, identity substitution, parameter mutation, replay, retry, crash and stale decisions.
Record actual external/canonical effects independently of Engine return values.
Cross-check every effect against the oracle authorization set at the moment the effect became eligible.
Attack the Engine directly as well as through generated tools so tool hiding is not credited as the only defense.
Inject tool-overexposure, mutable-gated-input and identity-confusion mutants; require detection.

oracle: Pure capability/effect model built from frozen principal, authority, policy and resource fixtures, plus an effect meter that reads external/canonical ground truth rather than candidate logs.
baseline: Strong conventional typed API/tool surface with least-privilege credentials and independent service-side authorization, used contextually here and as the full comparator in H30.

support_if: 0 forbidden committed effects across the frozen adversarial corpus.
Direct Engine backstop independently rejects every tool-surface denial tested.
reject_if: Any forbidden effect, authority expansion or post-authorization gated-input substitution commits through a supported path.
inconclusive_if: Fewer than 10,000 unique sequences run, effect ground truth is not independently observed, or attack coverage omits A1/A2/A8.
invalid_if: The authority oracle imports candidate enforcement code, the effect meter trusts candidate success responses, or the corpus excludes public calls discovered after freeze.

python_hypothesis_role.strategy: RuleBasedStateMachine generates identities, tools, actions, parameter mutations, replay/retry/crash and direct Engine calls, shrinking any forbidden effect to a minimal sequence.
python_hypothesis_role.mutation_proof: Plant an identity-substitution bug, a mutable-gated-input bug and an Engine gate bypass; all must be killed.

stop_conditions: A single real forbidden effect rejects the current containment design; fix it only in a new candidate experiment version rather than weakening the oracle.
